scope: ADR 1190 operation-level control rationale and its successors in quorra-confined; host policy, user operations, worker boundary, and evidence for saving/editing.

source_evidence.claim: ADR 1190 says the confined host owes a control exactly when it can perform an operation, but its inventory says it performs no form fill or save.
ADR 1592 adds Tab field traversal, text entry, commit and Ctrl+S save to the confined host.
source_evidence.status: built successor; no reassessment of document restriction controls

source_evidence.claim: ADR 1987 adds pointer press/release; checkbox clicks can fill a field, and media handoff is restrictable.
source_evidence.status: built successor; establishes further operations but retains no-level posture

implementation.claim: The confined worker is opened without a Command::Restrict; its default RestrictionPolicy is Off for each operation (except OverridePreference, which defaults Warn).
The confined CLI carries link, remote-document, submission and launched-document settings; document restrictions are explicitly refused by name and remain Off.
Unexpected Event::Asking is reported as unanswerable and answered proceed=false; current Off default is expected to prevent this event for document restrictions.
implementation.status: fail-closed branch; no direct host regression assertion located

implementation.claim: Ctrl+S dispatches Command::Save; Event::Saved bytes are written to input.with_extension("edited.pdf") and write errors are printed.
A save is a policy-controlled core operation and is directly invoked by the user in this host.

assertions.claim: The non-gating UI drive's field_commit step runs in all four windows, types/commits values, presses Ctrl+S, parses the resulting .edited.pdf and checks literal field values and appearances.
assertions.strength: end-to-end UI plus worker-to-host disk output and parsed-document content; it removes a previous target before run

assertions.claim: The confined worker test directly sends Command::Save and checks returned Event::Saved bytes retain the original document prefix.
assertions.strength: worker boundary only; does not exercise host disk path

assertions.claim: Host unit tests exercise link, remote-file and submission questions; no write_saved/path-collision/source-preservation host test was located.
assertions.strength: reviewed current tests file; absence is not itself a requirement defect

verdict: No confirmed document-restriction behavior defect under the stated project policy: Off is the explicit reader-favoring default and the reader can turn restrictions off. ADR 1190's operation-level rule remains a useful rule, but its assertion that no form-fill/save operations exist is stale after ADR 1592 (and some interaction premises are stale after ADR 1987). The successors implement those operations without revisiting document restriction-level configuration. Whether this confined host should expose non-Off document restriction levels is an explicit policy/ADR reconciliation question, not a standards finding. A Ctrl+S confirmation is not inferred: save is a direct user action. Current UI-drive evidence covers a typical source filename and fresh target, but not preservation of an existing target, source preservation, or surfaced disk-write failures. A standalone Rust Path::with_extension check confirms foo.edited.pdf maps to foo.edited.edited.pdf, so it does not alias the source.
